file.content:
### Committed Checkpoints

Branch: `entire/checkpoints/v1`

Committed checkpoints sync to exactly one git remote — the elected checkpoint
sync remote, resolved in this order:

1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` if set — fail-closed when it
   names a remote that is not configured (checkpoint sync is disabled until
   fixed, since this is explicit user intent).
2. `origin`, if configured.
3. The sole configured remote.
4. The first remote in `.git/config` order.

The branch's tracking config (`branch.<name>.pushRemote`,
`remote.pushDefault`, `branch.<name>.remote`) is deliberately **not** a tier.
Election is compared against the remote of the push being made, so electing
the tracking remote turns every push to a different remote into a silent
no-op — `git push <other> HEAD`, a `git clone -o base` whose checkpoints go to
a separately added `origin`, any repo with `remote.pushDefault` set. It would
also elect a remote the read paths cannot see, since `resume` and `explain`
resolve checkpoints through origin's remote-tracking refs.

For the fork setup where `origin` is an unpushable base repo, name the fork
explicitly with `checkpoint_push_remote` — the only form of it where the
checkpoints can also be read back.

The pre-push hook carries checkpoint data only when the push targets the
elected remote; pushes to any other remote or to a raw URL sync nothing, on
both the git-branch and git-refs backends (git-refs leaves its push queue
intact for the next elected-remote push). The dedicated `checkpoint_remote`
URL mode is exempt — it addresses a separate metadata store directly. `entire
status` shows the sync destination and how many checkpoints have not reached
it yet.

Metadata only, sharded by checkpoint ID. Supports **multiple sessions per checkpoint**:

```

input.new_string:
Committed checkpoints sync to exactly one git remote — the elected checkpoint
sync remote, resolved in this order:

1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` if set — fail-closed when it
   names a remote that is not configured (checkpoint sync is disabled until
   fixed, since this is explicit user intent).
2. The **captured** election, if its remote is still configured — fail-soft
   otherwise (capture is automatic state, so a renamed/removed remote falls
   through instead of disabling sync).
3. `origin`, if configured.
4. The sole configured remote.
5. The first remote in `.git/config` order.

**Capture** is how the election follows the user's actual push habit with
zero configuration: during pre-push, when the push target agrees with the
branch's declared push destination (`branch.<name>.pushRemote` →
`remote.pushDefault` → `branch.<name>.remote` — the config a bare `git push`
resolves through) and differs from the current election, that remote is
persisted as the captured election (git common dir,
`entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json`, list-shaped for the future multi-remote
set), a one-line stderr notice announces the change, and the same push carries
the checkpoints. Declaration alone never elects (the config-at-rest bug that
got the static tracking tier dropped in `74e239a9` — it turned pushes to every
other remote into silent no-ops, e.g. `git clone -o base` pushing a separately
added `origin`); a bare push to an undeclared remote never elects either (the
pre-single-remote transcript leak). Phase-1 rules: at most one captured
remote, and the first capture sticks — a mixed-habit repo whose branches push
two remotes must not flip the election per push. An explicit
`checkpoint_push_remote` always outranks and disables capture. See
`strategy/checkpoint_sync_capture.go`.

For the fork setup where `origin` is an unpushable base repo, capture elects
the fork automatically on the first tracked push; `checkpoint_push_remote`
remains the explicit override.

The single-remote election (ENT-1451) guesses the sync destination from

whose branches push a non-origin remote had checkpoints strand locally
until they hand-configured checkpoint_push_remote. First user report
landed the day after v0.10.0 shipped.

configuration: during pre-push, a push whose target agrees with the
branch's declared push destination (branch.<name>.pushRemote →
remote.pushDefault → branch.<name>.remote — the config a bare `git push`
resolves through) and differs from the current election persists that
remote as the captured election, announces it on stderr, and the same
push carries the checkpoints. The captured tier sits between the
explicit setting and origin, and is fail-soft: a captured remote that
was renamed or removed falls through to the default tiers instead of
disabling sync.

Neither signal elects alone. Declaration without a push is the
config-at-rest bug that got the static tracking tier dropped (74e239a9:
a clone -o base stranded every origin push); a push without declaration
is the pre-single-remote transcript leak (one-off `git push upstream`
must never publish transcripts). Capture acts only on their
intersection.

Phase-1 rules: at most one captured remote and the first capture sticks,
so a mixed-habit repo whose branches push two remotes cannot flip the
election on every push. The state file is list-shaped from day one so
the multi-remote set (per-remote push-queue tracking) needs no
migration. An explicit checkpoint_push_remote outranks and disables
capture.

The existing single-remote integration tests set up their gated remote
with `push -u`, which under capture is a declared destination — their
setups now reset tracking so they keep pinning the undeclared-one-off
shape, and TestCheckpointSyncRemote_BranchTrackingDoesNotReroute is
split into its two surviving truths: tracking alone still never reroutes
(the 74e239a9 regression pin), and a tracked push now legitimately
captures.

(#1956/#1951) lands; this PR must merge after it so captured non-origin
elections are readable end to end.

aiTitle: Review PRs and investigate checkpoint push remote logic

input.content:
## Problem

The single-remote election (ENT-1451, v0.10.0) guesses the checkpoint sync destination from config at rest: `checkpoint_push_remote` -> `origin` -> sole -> first in `.git/config`. A user whose branches push a non-origin remote loses that election to a dormant origin, so every push is gated and checkpoints strand locally until they discover and hand-configure `checkpoint_push_remote`. The first user report landed the day after release ("I have a bunch of repos where the git remote I push to isn't called origin. It looks like this means I no longer push checkpoints.").

#1893 fixed "checkpoints sync where they shouldn't" (transcript fan-out) but left "checkpoints don't sync where they should" as an opt-in config remedy. This PR is the second half.

## Change

**Capture**: during pre-push, a push whose target agrees with the branch's declared push destination (`branch.<name>.pushRemote` -> `remote.pushDefault` -> `branch.<name>.remote` — the config a bare `git push` resolves through) and differs from the current election persists that remote as the **captured election**, announces it on stderr, and the same push carries the checkpoints:

```
[entire] Checkpoints now sync to "fork" — the remote your branch pushes to. Override with strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote in .entire/settings.local.json.
```

New election precedence: explicit setting (fail-closed, unchanged) -> **captured** (fail-soft: a renamed/removed captured remote falls through instead of disabling sync) -> origin -> sole -> first.

**Neither signal elects alone.** Declaration without a push is the config-at-rest bug that got the static tracking tier dropped pre-merge in #1893 (`74e239a9`: a `clone -o base` stranded every origin push — pinned by `TestCheckpointSyncRemote_TrackingAloneDoesNotReroute`); a push without declaration is the pre-#1893 transcript leak (a one-off `git push upstream` for a PR must never publish transcripts). Capture acts only on their intersection.

**Phase-1 rules** (multi-remote set is the follow-up):
- At most one captured remote; **first capture sticks** — a mixed-habit repo whose branches push two remotes cannot flip the election per push.
- State is list-shaped from day one (`.git/entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json`, `{"remotes":[...]}`) so lifting the cap needs no migration.
- Explicit `checkpoint_push_remote` outranks and disables capture; dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL mode and `push_sessions: false` never reach it.
- `entire status` renders the source: `fork (captured from your pushes)`; `--json` reports `checkpoint_sync_remote_source: "captured"`.

## Test changes worth reviewer attention

The existing single-remote integration tests set up their gated remote with `push -u`, which under capture is a *declared* destination — pushing it now legitimately re-elects. Their setups reset tracking (`setBranchTrackingRemote`) so they keep pinning the undeclared-one-off shape, and `TestCheckpointSyncRemote_BranchTrackingDoesNotReroute` is split into its two surviving truths:

- `TrackingAloneDoesNotReroute`: a tracked-but-never-pushed remote still never receives data and captures nothing (the `74e239a9` regression pin).
- `TrackedPushCapturesElection`: the fork topology end to end — capture fires, the same push delivers, origin is gated thereafter, status reports `captured`.

Unit: captured-tier precedence table, capture predicate table (declaration precedence, already-elected no-op, first-capture-sticks, config disable, raw-URL), corrupt/missing state fail-soft.

## Sequencing

**Merge after #1956 -> #1951.** Reads still resolve through origin until that stack lands; merging capture first would route checkpoints to a remote other clones cannot read from. Nothing in this diff depends on the stack's code — the read chain picks up the captured election automatically once both exist.

Not done here, deliberately: multi-remote set (needs per-remote push-queue state — ENT-1494's rescope), capture from pushed refspecs rather than HEAD's branch (hook doesn't plumb stdin refspecs; a miss is conservative), `entire clean` leaving the state file (parity with the push-queue file).

## Testing

`mise run fmt` clean, `mise run lint` 0 issues, full unit suite (8,846), full integration suite (475), Vogon canary — all green.

content.text:
Phase 1 is built, verified, and up as **draft PR #1991**: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1991

**What shipped on the branch** (`feat/checkpoint-sync-capture`, own worktree, off latest main):

- **`strategy/checkpoint_sync_capture.go`** — the whole feature: list-shaped state file in the git common dir (`entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json`), the capture trigger (push target must agree with the branch's declared push destination: `branch.pushRemote` → `remote.pushDefault` → `branch.remote`), the stderr announcement pointing at `settings.local.json`, and atomic fail-soft persistence.
- **Resolver**: new `captured` tier between the explicit setting and origin — fail-soft (a renamed captured remote falls through instead of disabling sync, unlike the fail-closed explicit setting).
- **`prePush`**: capture runs just before the gate, so the electing push is also the first push that carries the checkpoints.
- **Status**: `Checkpoints sync to: fork (captured from your pushes)`, JSON source `captured`.
- **Docs**: election section rewritten in `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and CLAUDE.md.

**Tests** (TDD both layers — watched each fail first): 13 new unit subtests covering the tier precedence and every capture guard, plus integration scenarios for the fork topology end-to-end (capture fires, same push delivers, origin gated afterward, status reports `captured`), the `clone -o base` immunity pin, and the undeclared one-off. One design-consequence worth knowing: the existing gate tests set up remotes with `push -u`, which under capture *is* a declaration — so their setups now reset tracking, and `BranchTrackingDoesNotReroute` was split into its two surviving truths (tracking alone never reroutes; tracking + push captures). Full unit (8,846), full integration (475), and the Vogon canary are all green; lint 0 issues.

**Two things to know:**
1. It's a **draft** because of the agreed merge order — after #1956 → #1951, so captured non-origin elections are readable end-to-end. The code has no dependency on the stack; only the merge does.
2. One transient hiccup mid-commit: backticks in my commit message got executed as shell substitution (a stray bare `git push` ran and failed harmlessly on upstream mismatch — nothing was pushed by it). The message was amended clean before the real push.

The full arc is now in flight: #1987 (hint, review-complete) → #1956/#1951 (reads follow election, your open stack) → #1991 (capture, draft) — with phase 2 (the consented multi-remote set, per-remote queue state) scoped in the PR body as the ENT-1494 rescope.

Replacement is #1664 (off main): `--timeout` default 20m → 0/none; reviewers run until done like directly-invoked skills; judge keeps its own 5m default via `judgeTimeoutArg`. Key engineering finding: NO inactivity watchdog is possible — legit review subagents run 12+ min with zero parent stdout, so headless children have no liveness signal distinguishing quiet-working from hung. **A/B verified (controlled, same branch/skills): plain claude session 9m57s vs entire review 9m08s — no wrapper tax; duration is the task.**

21

content.text:
All fixed — the joke resolved itself into a nice bug report:

**What happened:** the capture commit *did* get an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer (prepare-commit-msg stamps one regardless), but it was **dangling** — post-commit condensation matches the session by `worktree_path`, this session is bound to `.worktrees/pr-review`, so in `.worktrees/checkpoint-capture` it found no session and wrote no checkpoint. `explain` on that ID returned "no checkpoint found" while the #1987 commits (made in this session's own worktree) condensed normally with the full session.

**The fix** (my documented retro-attach procedure, third time it's been needed): backed up the session state, repointed `worktree_path` + `worktree_id` at the capture worktree, replayed the commit via `reset --soft` + re-commit so the hooks fired with the session visible, restored the state, force-pushed. PR #1991 now sits on `2661867ad` with checkpoint `01KZZ0TAD9RHHGXWN4VX18CV68` carrying this whole session — verified via `explain`. The force-push was safe: draft, unreviewed, single commit, and the old commit's linkage was precisely what didn't exist.

Two things worth taking away:

1. **New failure shape for the memory books** (recorded): this gap used to present as *missing trailer*; since the schema evolved it presents as *trailer present but dangling* — so "commit has a trailer" is no longer proof of linkage; `entire checkpoint explain <trailer>` is.
2. **The product gap itself is now three-for-three** on multi-worktree agent sessions (#1647, #1287, now #1991) — and it's adjacent to the very thing we spent today on: sessions silently not attaching in sibling worktrees is the read/write-side cousin of checkpoints silently not syncing to non-elected remotes. Same pattern — a binding chosen from state-at-rest (`worktree_path` at session start) disagreeing with observed behavior (where the commit actually happens). If you want, that's worth filing as its own issue with today's capture design as prior art for the fix shape.

> Same-remote-as-the-push was the old behavior, and it's what the earlier round of complaints was about — every push carried your session transcripts with it, so a one-off `git push upstream` for a PR published them somewhere you can't unpublish. So beyond the hint, I just built the conditional version of what you're describing: a push to the remote your branch is configured to push (the one a bare `git push` uses) now elects that remote for checkpoints automatically and announces it. Your repos work again with zero config, and a one-off push to someone else's remote still can't take your transcripts with it. https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1046
>
> Until that lands, the `settings.local.json` override above is the fix.

A couple of notes on framing, in case you want to trim:

- The middle paragraph is the real answer to his question — it concedes his point ("least surprise says push target should matter") while explaining the one condition that makes it safe (declared destination, not any push). That's the honest shape: he was right about the what, the guard is the why.
- I'd keep the last line — Pat has repos broken *today*, and capture merges behind the read stack, so the interim fix still matters to him.

content.text:
Full findings — and the diagnosis I gave you yesterday was partly wrong, which is itself part of the answer:

## What actually happened to PR #1991's session attach

The dangling trailer was **not** the cross-worktree gap. Log forensics (`.entire/logs/entire.log` at 19:08:47) show prepare-commit-msg linked that commit to a session called **`sessC`** — a *Cursor* fixture session, phase `ended`, kind `imported`. It stamped sessC's checkpoint ID; condensation had nothing real to condense; the trailer dangled.

Where sessC came from: `agentimport_test.go` builds everything in `t.TempDir()` but **never `t.Chdir`s**, and `session.NewStateStore(ctx)` (`session/state.go:559`) resolves the git common dir **from CWD**. So when I ran `mise run test` from the capture worktree at 19:02, nine fixture sessions (`sess1`–`sess3`, `sessC`, `sess-anchor`, …) were upserted into the **real** `.git/entire-sessions/` — exactly the violation the CLAUDE.md testing rules warn about, and the session store has no `go test` safety net the way `userdirs`/`tokenstore` do. Six minutes later my commit picked the poison fixture. I've quarantined all nine files.

## So: the gaps that actually need addressing

1. **The test leak** (concrete, ours, trivial): `agentimport_test.go` needs `t.Chdir(repoDir)` or `NewStateStoreWithDir`; better, give the session state store the same in-process `go test` fallback the other stores have, so *no* future test can pollute a real repo.
2. **Commit-linking doesn't exclude non-linkable sessions**: an `ended`, `imported` session should never be chosen for a fresh commit's trailer. One filter in `findSessionsForWorktree`/its callers.
3. **No stamp→condense reconciliation**: prepare-commit-msg can stamp an ID whose checkpoint is never written, and nothing warns or repairs — trailer presence masquerades as linkage. A doctor check ("trailers on recent commits that resolve to no checkpoint") would surface it.

## Why the previous PRs/trails didn't resolve it

Because each fixed a different layer, and yesterday's instance was a layer none of them touch: the **cross-worktree gap itself is largely fixed on main** — `findSessionsForWorktree` has had a sibling-worktree fallback since ~#1852 (matches sessions from one other worktree; ambiguity across several warns and declines). My July-era memory predated that, which is why I reached for the manual retro-attach. Without the sessC poisoning, yesterday's commit would likely have linked to this session automatically via that fallback. The remaining true residuals of the old gap are the ambiguous-multi-worktree case (declines with only a log Warn) and `session adopt` being a manual remedy — but neither was yesterday's culprit.

Want me to fix gap 1 (and optionally 2) now? Both are small; gap 3 is doctor-recovery-shaped and pairs naturally with the unplanned "PR 2" from the sync-remote spec.

content.text:
Three straight answers:

**1. Dangling trailers — no, not handled.** Nothing in the product detects or repairs them; that's exactly gap 3. The specific one on #1991 no longer exists (the force-push replaced the commit entirely), but any dangling trailer already in anyone's history sits there silently — `explain` just says "no checkpoint found" with no hint that it's a stamp-without-condense artifact, and no doctor check hunts for them. Fix 3 is what would make them *handled* (detect: trailers on recent commits resolving to no checkpoint; repair where the session still exists locally).

**2. Do fixes 1–3 cover what we found — yes, each maps to one layer of yesterday's failure:**
- **Fix 1** (test isolation / go-test safety net for the session store) removes the root cause — no pollution, no sessC, yesterday's commit links correctly via the existing sibling-worktree fallback.
- **Fix 2** (exclude `imported`/`ended` sessions from commit-linking) makes the class un-exploitable — even if junk lands in `.git/entire-sessions/` some other way, it can't be chosen for a fresh commit.
- **Fix 3** turns the failure from invisible into diagnosed, for instances that slip through anyway.

What they deliberately *don't* cover: the ambiguous multi-worktree case still declines to link with only a log-level Warn (a stderr hint there would match the #1987 pattern), and `session adopt` stays manual. No PID or ancestry machinery exists anywhere in the codebase — so here's the scope for the actual cause-level fix, which makes your invariant real: **an agent-made commit always attaches to the session that made it, deterministically, no inference.**

## The design: identity-based linking (process ancestry)

The insight yesterday's incident proves: when *I* committed in the capture worktree, the git hook process was a **descendant of my Claude Code process**. The system didn't need to guess by worktree — the answer was in the process tree the whole time. Two pieces:

**1. Record identity at session start.** Entire's agent hooks (SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit) already run as children of the agent process. The hook walks its parent chain, finds the agent process, and records `agent_pid` + process start time (start time guards against PID reuse) in the session state. ~30 lines plus a new state field.

**2. Resolve identity at commit time.** `prepare-commit-msg`/`post-commit` walk *their* ancestry (git ← tool shell ← agent). An ancestor matching a recorded `agent_pid`+start-time **is** the committing session — linked regardless of worktree, worktree matching never consulted. Yesterday: git's ancestry contained my Claude process → my session, deterministic, done.

**The new machinery** is a cross-platform ancestry walker (macOS `sysctl KERN_PROC`, Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat`, Windows toolhelp snapshot) — ~150 lines, the only genuinely new subsystem. Integration tests get it almost free: the harness process that spawns `entire hooks git ...` can register *itself* as the agent PID.

**Fallback hierarchy** (this is where the PR-A fixes stop being "not the cause" and become the right supporting layers):
1. Ancestry match → that session, any worktree. (Agent commits — the invariant, always.)
2. No agent in ancestry (a human committing in a terminal) → worktree match with the hygiene fixes: imported sessions excluded, liveness tiebreak, stderr hint on genuine ambiguity.
3. Detached/backgrounded agent processes (setsid-style) lose ancestry → degrade to tier 2. Documented, rare.

**One real design decision inside it — your "adopt should be automatic":** when ancestry says session-in-worktree-A committed in worktree B, do we (a) **guest-link** — condense and attach without moving the session, or (b) **auto-adopt** — move `worktree_path` to B? I recommend **guest-link for v1**: yesterday I committed *once* in a sibling while continuing to live in pr-review — auto-adopt would have moved the session away and then bounced it back on my next pr-review commit, churning worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow branches) that the code deliberately only mutates for the session's own worktree. Guest-link gives you the invariant you actually asked for (always attached) without the state churn; auto-adopt can be layered later if a session's commits *consistently* land elsewhere. The one subtlety guest-link must honor: skip the `BaseCommit`/shadow-branch mutations for foreign-worktree condensation (the `findExactSessionsForWorktree` contract already draws exactly this line).

- **PR A (hygiene, small, ~40 prod lines):** test-leak fix + fail-loud store guard, imported-session exclusion, liveness tiebreak + stderr hint. Ships the human-commit fallback and makes pollution impossible. Off latest main, buildable today.

content.text:
Correct — `adopt` isn't touched. Not one line. The fix is entirely in **how a commit finds its session**, which today is the only reason you ever needed adopt as a repair tool.

The mechanism, plainly:

**Today:** when you (or an agent) run `git commit`, entire's commit hooks ask "which session does this commit belong to?" and answer by comparing paths — "which session state file has `worktree_path` equal to the directory this commit is happening in?" That's inference from bookkeeping, and it breaks whenever the bookkeeping and reality diverge: agent bound to worktree A commits in worktree B → no match (or worse, a wrong match, like the sessC fixture) → linkage lost → you reach for adopt or manual JSON surgery to repair it.

**After the fix:** the hooks answer the same question by looking at **who is running the commit**. Two parts:

1. When a session starts, its hook records the agent's process ID (plus process start time, so a recycled PID can't impersonate) into the session state. The hook is a child of the agent, so it can just look up its own parent — nothing new for agents to do.
2. When a commit happens, the commit hook walks *its* parent processes: `git` ← the shell that ran it ← ... ← the agent. If any ancestor is a recorded agent process, that session **is** the answer — a fact about the process tree, not a guess from paths. Worktree becomes irrelevant for agent commits.

The old worktree matching stays as the fallback for commits with no agent in their ancestry (you committing by hand in a terminal) — and gets the hygiene hardening (imported fixtures can't match, live sessions beat days-idle ones, ambiguity says so on stderr instead of a buried log line).

So adopt doesn't change; **its repair job evaporates** because the thing it was repairing can't break anymore for agent commits. What's left of adopt is what it was actually designed for — deliberately moving a session's home to another repo/worktree — not fixing linkage after the fact.

Location: `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json`

Stored in git common dir (shared across worktrees). Tracks active session info.

The state records `Branch` — the branch HEAD pointed at on the session's last turn
(captured each turn start, so it follows branches created/renamed after the
session began). `entire resume` (bare, no arg) uses it to list stopped sessions
and map each back to its branch; for sessions recorded before the field existed
it falls back to deriving the branch from the session's last checkpoint ID found
in branch-only commit trailers.

`entire session adopt` moves an active session from a source repo or worktree
into the current worktree. Adoption preserves the live transcript path, validates
that the source state still belongs to the requested source worktree, rewrites
the session's branch/worktree/base metadata to the target, clears target-local
checkpoint windows and checkpoint IDs, and snapshots the target's current file
changes so the next commit can link to the adopted session.

`entire session adopt` moves an active session from a source repo or worktree
into the current worktree. Adoption preserves the live transcript path, validates
that the source state still belongs to the requested source worktree, rewrites
the session's branch/worktree/base metadata to the target, clears target-local
checkpoint windows and checkpoint IDs, and snapshots the target's current file
changes so the next commit can link to the adopted session.

#### Commit-to-session linking

The commit hooks (prepare-commit-msg / post-commit) resolve which sessions a
commit belongs to via `findSessionsForCommitLinking`
(`strategy/session_identity.go`): the **worktree-matched set** (every session
with pending content in the commit's worktree — concurrent sessions interleave
by design) **plus the identity-matched session** when the committing process's
ancestry names one that path matching missed.

**Identity matching**: at session start the hook records its nearest process
ancestors (pid + start time; the agent process is among them, since agents run
hooks as children) in `SessionState.AgentAncestry`. At commit time the hook
walks its own ancestry (git ← tool shell ← agent) and matches those refs —
nearest ancestor wins, ties go to the most recently interacting session, and
start times guard against PID reuse. This makes an agent-made commit link to
its own session **in any worktree**, with no bookkeeping to drift. A commit
identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is **guest-linked**: it
condenses and links, but never mutates worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`,
shadow-branch realignment) — those follow only the session's own worktree HEAD.

**Worktree matching** (the fallback, for commits with no recorded agent in
their ancestry — human commits, detached runners): exact `WorktreePath` match
first, then sessions from a sibling worktree of the same repo, provided they
resolve to a single worktree. Imported sessions (`Kind=imported`) never link —
they are historical records. When candidates span several worktrees, sessions
that interacted within the last 15 minutes are preferred; if a single live
worktree remains it links, otherwise the hook declines with a stderr hint
naming `entire session adopt` (two genuinely live sessions in different
worktrees are never guessed between).

Under `go test`, the session state store refuses to open outside the temp
root (`session.NewStateStore`), so a test missing repo isolation fails loudly
instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo's `.git/entire-sessions`
— leaked fixtures once hijacked commit linking and produced a dangling
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

input.content:
feat(strategy): link commits to sessions by process identity

Commit-to-session linking guessed by worktree path: the commit hooks
matched SessionState.WorktreePath against the commit's worktree. Any
drift between that bookkeeping and reality lost the linkage — an agent
committing in a sibling worktree produced an unlinked commit, or worse:
with a poisoned state dir, a wrong link. Both happened for real (three
retro-attach incidents; most recently a leaked test fixture session,
sessC, was linked to a commit and stamped a dangling trailer whose
checkpoint was never written).

Identity-first linking removes the guessing for agent commits. At
session start the hook records its nearest process ancestors
(pid + start time; the agent process is among them, since agents run
hooks as children) in SessionState.AgentAncestry. At commit time the
hook walks its own ancestry (git <- tool shell <- agent) and matches
those refs: nearest ancestor wins, ties go to the most recently
interacting session, start times guard against PID reuse. The identity
match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement —
a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree,
and identity adds the one that path matching missed.

A commit identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is
guest-linked: condensed and linked, but worktree-coupled state
(BaseCommit, shadow-branch realignment) is never mutated from a foreign
worktree — shadow branches are keyed by BaseCommit + WorktreeID, and
the session's next home commit must still match.

The worktree fallback (human commits, severed process trees) is
hardened in the same pass:

- Imported sessions never link: they are historical records, and a
  leaked imported fixture is exactly what hijacked the sessC commit.
- Multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to sessions that interacted
  within the last 15 minutes; a single live worktree links, two live
  worktrees still decline — now with a stderr hint naming
  'entire session adopt' instead of only a log-level warning.

And the leak that poisoned the state dir is closed at both ends:
agent import scopes its session-state store to the repo being imported
into (new session.NewStateStoreForWorktree) instead of the process CWD,
and under 'go test' the CWD-resolved store refuses to open outside the
temp root, so any future non-isolated test fails loudly instead of
writing fixtures into a developer's real .git/entire-sessions. The full
unit suite passes with the guard on — the agentimport tests were the
only leakers.

New internal/proctree package: cross-platform process ancestry
(darwin sysctl, linux /proc, windows toolhelp) with pid+starttime
identity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

input.content:
## Problem

Commit-to-session linking guesses by worktree path: the commit hooks match `SessionState.WorktreePath` against the commit's worktree. Any drift between bookkeeping and reality loses the linkage. This has bitten three times (PR #1647, PR #1287, PR #1991): an agent committing in a sibling worktree gets an unlinked commit — or, with a poisoned state dir, a **wrong** link. The latest instance: `agentimport` tests missing repo isolation leaked fixture sessions (`sessC` et al.) into the developer's real `.git/entire-sessions`; prepare-commit-msg linked a commit to the `sessC` fixture and stamped a trailer whose checkpoint was never written — a dangling trailer, repaired only by manual session-state surgery.

## Change

**Identity-first linking.** An agent-made commit is attributed by *who made it*, not *where it happened*:

- Session-start hooks record their nearest process ancestors (pid + start time + exe) in `SessionState.AgentAncestry` — the agent process is among them, since agents run hooks as children. New `internal/proctree` package resolves ancestry cross-platform (darwin sysctl, linux `/proc`, windows toolhelp); pid+starttime pairs survive PID reuse.
- Commit hooks walk their own ancestry (git ← tool shell ← agent) and match those refs: nearest ancestor wins, ties go to the most recently interacting session. The match is **unioned** with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement — a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree (concurrent sessions interleave by design), and identity adds the one path matching missed.
- **Guest-linking:** a commit identity-matched outside the session's home worktree condenses and links, but never mutates worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment — keyed by BaseCommit + WorktreeID) from a foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). The session's next home-worktree commit still matches.

Net effect: **an agent commit links to its session in any worktree, automatically** — no `session adopt`, no retro-attach. `adopt` shrinks to its migration role.

**Hardened worktree fallback** (human commits, severed process trees):
- Imported sessions never link (historical records; a leaked imported fixture is exactly what hijacked the sessC commit).
- Multi-worktree ambiguity filters to sessions that interacted within 15 minutes: one live worktree links; two live worktrees still decline — never guess — but now say so on **stderr with the remedy** (`entire session adopt`) instead of a log-level warning only (#1852's gap).

**Leak closed at both ends:**
- `agentimport` scopes its session-state writes to the repo being imported into (new `session.NewStateStoreForWorktree`) instead of the process CWD — a production bug, not just a test bug.
- Under `go test`, the CWD-resolved `session.NewStateStore` refuses to open outside the temp root, so any future non-isolated test **fails loudly** instead of writing fixtures into a real repo. The full unit suite (8,967) passes with the guard on — the agentimport tests were the only leakers in the repo.

## Testing

- `internal/proctree`: real-process tests incl. a helper-process round-trip proving a child sees its parent's pid+starttime identity; cross-compiled and vetted for linux/windows.
- Strategy unit: ancestry recording at session init; identity matching (worktree-independence, PID-reuse rejection, imported exclusion, latest-interaction tiebreak); union semantics (guest added, local set preserved, fallback intact); imported-never-links; liveness disambiguation + audible decline.
- Session/agentimport: store guard (refuses real repo under test, allows temp), repo-scoped import state.
- `mise run fmt` clean, `mise run lint` 0 issues, full unit suite 8,967 pass, integration suite + Vogon canary green.

## Notes for reviewers

- `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` and the condensation-success path both gate on `isSessionHomeWorktree` — same contract `postCommitUpdateBaseCommitOnly` already documented for exact matches.
- Guest-linked condensation captures transcript + linkage; file attribution for foreign-worktree edits stays scoped as before (guest FilesTouched are home-relative). Documented as the v1 boundary.
- Detached/backgrounded agent processes (severed trees) degrade to the hardened worktree fallback.
- The 15-minute liveness window is a named constant (`recentSessionWindow`); value is a judgment call, flag if you'd pick differently.

content.text:
Done. **PR #2013: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2013**

The cause fix is shipped — commits link to sessions by **who made them** (process ancestry), not where they happened:

**What's in it:**
- **`internal/proctree`** — cross-platform ancestry walker (darwin sysctl, linux `/proc`, windows toolhelp), with pid+start-time identity so a recycled PID can't impersonate a dead agent. Includes a helper-process round-trip test proving a real child sees its parent's identity.
- **Recording**: session-start hooks store their nearest 3 process ancestors in `SessionState.AgentAncestry` — the agent is among them since agents run hooks as children.
- **Resolution**: commit hooks walk their own ancestry and match; the identity hit is **unioned** with the worktree-matched set (a mid-build correction — replacing the set would have dropped concurrent local sessions from the commit, which the full suite caught). Guest-linked commits condense and link but never mutate `BaseCommit`/shadow-branch state from a foreign worktree.
- **Fallback hardening**: imported sessions never link (the sessC class is dead even if junk lands in the state dir again), multi-worktree ambiguity resolves by 15-minute liveness, and a genuine two-live-session tie declines *audibly* with a stderr hint naming `session adopt`.
- **Leak closed at both ends**: agentimport writes session state to the repo being imported into (that was a production bug, not just test hygiene), and under `go test` the store refuses to open outside the temp root — the 8,967-test suite passes with the guard on, confirming agentimport was the only leaker.

**Verification**: lint 0 issues, full unit + integration (480) + Vogon canary all green.

One last poetic beat: the PR's own commit needed one final manual retro-attach — the *installed* binary predates the fix, session bound to `pr-review`, commit made in `session-identity`. Verified the replayed commit's checkpoint actually resolves (`explain` → this session, not dangling). Once #2013 merges and ships, that procedure goes in the drawer for good.

content.content:
1	package strategy
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"log/slog"
6	
7		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/internal/proctree"
8		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
9		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
10	)
11	
12	// agentAncestryDepth is how many ancestors the session-start hook records in
13	// SessionState.AgentAncestry. The chain above the hook is (shell that ran the
14	// hook) → agent → (terminal shell / supervisor); three levels reliably
15	// includes the agent process while staying below system-wide ancestors
16	// (terminal multiplexers, init) that would make unrelated processes look
17	// related.
18	const agentAncestryDepth = 3
19	
20	// commitAncestryDepth is how far the commit hook walks its own ancestry when
21	// matching — deeper than the recording depth because agents interpose shells
22	// and wrappers between themselves and the git subprocess (hook ← git ← tool
23	// shell(s) ← agent ← ...).
24	const commitAncestryDepth = 12
25	
26	// findSessionsForCommitLinking resolves which sessions a commit belongs to:
27	// the worktree-matched set (a commit captures the worktree's content, so
28	// every session with pending content here belongs in it — concurrent
29	// sessions interleave by design) PLUS the identity-matched session when the
30	// committing process's ancestry names one that worktree matching missed.
31	// The identity union is what makes an agent-made commit immune to worktree
32	// bookkeeping drift: an agent committing in a sibling worktree still links

This ensures restore/rewind works after repo relocation or across machines.

content.text:
# Comprehensive PR Review

Run a comprehensive pull request review using multiple specialized agents, each focusing on a different aspect of code quality.

**Review Aspects (optional):** "2013"

## Review Workflow:

1. **Determine Review Scope**
   - Check git status to identify changed files
   - Parse arguments to see if user requested specific review aspects
   - Default: Run all applicable reviews

2. **Available Review Aspects:**

   - **comments** - Analyze code comment accuracy and maintainability
   - **tests** - Review test coverage quality and completeness
   - **errors** - Check error handling for silent failures
   - **types** - Analyze type design and invariants (if new types added)
   - **code** - General code review for project guidelines
   - **simplify** - Simplify code for clarity and maintainability
   - **all** - Run all applicable reviews (default)

3. **Identify Changed Files**
   - Run `git diff --name-only` to see modified files
   - Check if PR already exists: `gh pr view`
   - Identify file types and what reviews apply

4. **Determine Applicable Reviews**

   Based on changes:
   - **Always applicable**: code-reviewer (general quality)
   - **If test files changed**: pr-test-analyzer
   - **If comments/docs added**: comment-analyzer
   - **If error handling changed**: silent-failure-hunter
   - **If types added/modified**: type-design-analyzer
   - **After passing review**: code-simplifier (polish and refine)

5. **Launch Review Agents**

   **Sequential approach** (one at a time):
   - Easier to understand and act on
   - Each report is complete before next
   - Good for interactive review

   **Parallel approach** (user can request):
   - Launch all agents simultaneously
   - Faster for comprehensive review
   - Results come back together

6. **Aggregate Results**

   After agents complete, summarize:
   - **Critical Issues** (must fix before merge)
   - **Important Issues** (should fix)
   - **Suggestions** (nice to have)
   - **Positive Observations** (what's good)

7. **Provide Action Plan**

   Organize findings:
   ```markdown
   # PR Review Summary

   ## Critical Issues (X found)
   - [agent-name]: Issue description [file:line]

   ## Important Issues (X found)
   - [agent-name]: Issue description [file:line]

   ## Suggestions (X found)
   - [agent-name]: Suggestion [file:line]

   ## Strengths
   - What's well-done in this PR

   ## Recommended Action
   1. Fix critical issues first
   2. Address important issues
   3. Consider suggestions
   4. Re-run review after fixes
   ```

## Usage Examples:

**Full review (default):**
```
/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr
```

**Specific aspects:**
```
/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr tests errors
# Reviews only test coverage and error handling

/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr comments
# Reviews only code comments

/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr simplify
# Simplifies code after passing review
```

**Parallel review:**
```
/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr all parallel
# Launches all agents in parallel
```

## Agent Descriptions:

**comment-analyzer**:
- Verifies comment accuracy vs code
- Identifies comment rot
- Checks documentation completeness

**pr-test-analyzer**:
- Reviews behavioral test coverage
- Identifies critical gaps
- Evaluates test quality

**silent-failure-hunter**:
- Finds silent failures
- Reviews catch blocks
- Checks error logging

**type-design-analyzer**:
- Analyzes type encapsulation
- Reviews invariant expression
- Rates type design quality

**code-reviewer**:
- Checks CLAUDE.md compliance
- Detects bugs and issues
- Reviews general code quality

**code-simplifier**:
- Simplifies complex code
- Improves clarity and readability
- Applies project standards
- Preserves functionality

## Tips:

- **Run early**: Before creating PR, not after
- **Focus on changes**: Agents analyze git diff by default
- **Address critical first**: Fix high-priority issues before lower priority
- **Re-run after fixes**: Verify issues are resolved
- **Use specific reviews**: Target specific aspects when you know the concern

## Workflow Integration:

**Before committing:**
```
1. Write code
2. Run: /pr-review-toolkit:review-pr code errors
3. Fix any critical issues
4. Commit
```

**Before creating PR:**
```
1. Stage all changes
2. Run: /pr-review-toolkit:review-pr all
3. Address all critical and important issues
4. Run specific reviews again to verify
5. Create PR
```

**After PR feedback:**
```
1. Make requested changes
2. Run targeted reviews based on feedback
3. Verify issues are resolved
4. Push updates
```

## Notes:

- Agents run autonomously and return detailed reports
- Each agent focuses on its specialty for deep analysis
- Results are actionable with specific file:line references
- Agents use appropriate models for their complexity
- All agents available in `/agents` list

- Issue: The doc says nearest-ancestor-wins resolves "if two sessions recorded processes at different depths of this commit's ancestry (an agent vs. the terminal shell it runs in)". Since `AgentAncestry` is a new field in this PR, no legacy multi-ref/shell-ref states exist either. The parenthetical is a fossil from the pre-bugbot-fix design (raw chain recording) and now describes an unreachable state. - Suggestion: Replace the parenthetical with a reachable case, e.g. "(a nested agent vs. the outer agent that spawned it, or an agent vs. the terminal emulator recorded for a shell-script agent)".

**2. "Identity first ... then worktree matching" in both commit hooks contradicts the union semantics the callee documents and implements.**
- Location: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:406-409` (PrepareCommitMsg) and `manual_commit_hooks.go:928-930` (PostCommit)
- Issue: `findSessionsForCommitLinking` (session_identity.go:26-46) runs worktree matching *first* and unions the identity match in — its own doc says "PLUS", and there is no precedence: both sets always contribute. "Identity first ..., then worktree matching" reads as a fallback chain (try identity; if it fails, try worktree), which is wrong on both order and semantics. A maintainer trusting this comment would expect an identity hit to *suppress* worktree matches — the exact behavior the union was designed to avoid (it would drop concurrent same-worktree sessions from the commit). Line 407's "in the fallback" compounds it. The docs section paragraph 1 and the `findSessionsForCommitLinking` doc get this right; these two hook comments are the outliers.

We match by worktree (not BaseCommit) because ..." — keeping the PostCommit comment's excellent "must resolve the same way PrepareCommitMsg did" invariant, which is accurate and valuable.

**3. `findSessionByCommitAncestry` closing line: "(the caller falls back to worktree matching)".**
- Location: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_identity.go:63-64`
- Current state: Same union-vs-fallback tension as #2, from the other side. The caller doesn't "fall back" on nil — worktree matching already ran unconditionally; a nil here just means the set isn't augmented.
- Suggestion: "(the linking set is then the worktree-matched sessions alone)".

**4. Docs section labels worktree matching "the fallback, for commits with no recorded agent in their ancestry" — contradicting the union stated two paragraphs above.**
- Location: `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md:197-198`
- Current state: Paragraph 1 (lines 176-182) correctly says worktree-set **plus** identity match. Paragraph 3 then scopes worktree matching to "commits with no recorded agent in their ancestry — human commits, detached runners". In fact worktree matching supplies the linking sessions for the common case too: an agent committing in its *home* worktree links via the worktree set (identity is redundant there). Someone reading only paragraph 3 would conclude agent commits never use worktree matching.
- Suggestion: "**Worktree matching** (always computed; the sole mechanism for commits with no recorded agent in their ancestry — human commits, detached runners): ...". Same nuance applies to CLAUDE.md:683 ("Worktree matching stays as the fallback for commits with no agent ancestry"), though that bullet at least states UNIONED explicitly first. The bolded "identity-first" name in CLAUDE.md:683 is also mildly at odds with union semantics but self-corrects within the sentence.

**5. `AgentAncestry` field: doc says "only that one ref" but the type is a slice, with no explanation of the plural.**
- Location: `cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:128-138`
- Current state: The doc states a single-ref contract ("Deliberately only that one ref") that the type (`[]proctree.ProcessRef`) cannot enforce, and `refsContain` (session_identity.go:113-120) loops as if multiple refs were expected. Nothing writes more than one ref today, but nothing says *why* the field is plural — a future writer could append refs without tripping anything, silently reintroducing the exact false-match bug the doc warns about. Per house rule this doc is doing its job (stating a constraint code can't show), but it should close the loop on the type.
- Suggestion: Add one clause, e.g. "the field is a slice only for serialization headroom; writers must never record more than the single agent ref" — or make the type a single optional ref.

**6. "session-start hook" is slightly loose about where recording happens.**
- Location: `cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:129`, `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_identity.go:14-15` and `:131` , docs line 183
- Current state: `recordAgentAncestry` runs in `initializeSession` (manual_commit_session.go:621), reachable from the turn-start hook (manual_commit_hooks.go:2393) *and* from `ensureSessionInitialized` on SaveStep/SaveTaskStep (manual_commit_git.go:42, 193, 208) when turn-start didn't create the state. All call sites are agent-spawned hook processes, so the recorded ref is the same agent either way — the claim's substance holds; only the literal "session-start hook" is imprecise.
- Suggestion: Low priority; "the hook that initializes the session" would be exact.

**7. proctree package doc: "a recycled PID always comes with a new start time" — not strictly true across reboots on Linux.**
- Location: `cmd/entire/cli/internal/proctree/proctree.go:1-7`
- Current state: The units claims are all verified correct (darwin: `Sec*1_000_000 + Usec` = microseconds since epoch, proctree_darwin.go:36; linux: `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 = clock ticks since boot, proctree_linux.go:40-44; windows: creation FILETIME, proctree_windows.go:45), and the comparison-only contract is upheld — nothing interprets `StartTime`. - Location: `cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:607-631` (guard) vs `:585-605` (`NewStateStoreForWorktree`)
- Current state: The guard doc lists `NewStateStoreForWorktree` as one of the *remedies* for a failing test, implying it's a sanctioned escape hatch — but a test passing the developer's real repo root to it reproduces the original leak with no loud failure. The docs (sessions-and-checkpoints.md:210, CLAUDE.md:683) correctly scope the refusal to `NewStateStore`, so nothing is factually wrong; the gap is just undocumented.
- Suggestion: One sentence on `NewStateStoreForWorktree`: "not covered by the go-test isolation guard — callers pass an explicit root and own that choice."

## Recommended Removals

None. Every added comment carries rationale or a constraint the code cannot express; none merely restates code.

## Positive Findings

- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_identity.go:130-141` (`recordAgentAncestry`): exemplary — states the invariant (stop at first non-shell), the threat model (shared terminal falsely matching human commits), *and* the accepted residual (shell-script agents), which is exactly what a future maintainer needs before "improving" the walk depth.
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:1419-1427` and `:1477-1479` (guest-link BaseCommit guards): the "keyed by BaseCommit + WorktreeID" orphaning rationale is verified accurate against the shadow-branch naming scheme, and the cross-reference from `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` to `condenseAndUpdateState` avoids duplicating it.
- `cmd/entire/cli/internal/proctree/proctree_linux.go:12-16` (`statFields`): the last-`)` parse rationale (comm may contain spaces/parens) with field-index mapping is exactly right and matches the code's indices (`fields[1]` = ppid, `fields[19]` = starttime).
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_identity_test.go` regression headers name the specific incident each test guards (sessC dangling trailer, Cursor bugbot shell-recording, days-idle veto), per the project's test-comment discipline; the "Not parallel: uses t.Chdir()" annotations are all accurate.
- `cmd/entire/cli/agentimport/agentimport.go:303-304`: the added "scoped to repoRoot ... never the process CWD" sentence matches the `NewStateStoreForWorktree(ctx, opts.RepoRoot)` call exactly.
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_session.go:243-250` (`resolveWorktreeCandidates`): verified against control flow — single-worktree link, liveness filter (15 min matches `recentSessionWindow`), decline-with-stderr; the "days-idle stragglers must not veto" phrasing captures why the filter exists, not just what it does.

**Bottom line**: two fixes worth making before merge — the impossible "terminal shell" example in `session_identity.go:59` and the "Identity first, then worktree matching" fallback framing in both hook comments (`manual_commit_hooks.go:406`, `:928`), plus the matching "the fallback" label in `sessions-and-checkpoints.md:197`. Everything else is accurate or minor polish.</result>

<result># Test Coverage Analysis: PR #2013 (identity-first commit-to-session linking)

**1. Is identity linking exercised end-to-end/cross-process anywhere?** No test asserts it. But this makes identity and worktree matching always coincide, so the incidental exercise proves nothing: if `findSessionByCommitAncestry` silently returned nil forever (proctree failure, ancestry never recorded, JSON field renamed), every integration test still passes via the worktree fallback. Conversely an over-matching regression is equally invisible. **3. The skip *loop* never executes against real ancestry — in every test the first ancestor (go/gotestsum/test binary) is non-shell, so the loop returns immediately. Nothing verifies that on each platform a real `sh` ancestor's `Exe` field actually comes back in a form the table matches (basename vs full path vs truncated comm vs empty). - (a) guest direction: `BaseCommit`/`AttributionBaseCommit` must stay on A's head — catches removal of the gate, which orphans the shadow branch (keyed by BaseCommit + WorktreeID) and breaks the session's next home commit;
- (b) home direction: a session committed in its *own* worktree must still advance BaseCommit — catches `isSessionHomeWorktree` wrongly returning false (e.g. path-normalization drift like `/var` vs `/private/var` on macOS, or a resumed session whose `WorktreePath` was reconciled), which would silently freeze BaseCommit tracking for **every** session and break pre-identity behavior globally. **2. Full trailer flow with a guest in the set — rate 8.**
No test runs `PrepareCommitMsg` + `PostCommit` (even in-process, extending `phase_postcommit_test.go` or the worktree-session file) with an identity-matched guest whose shadow content lives in another worktree. Failures it would catch: guest condensation blowing up at ref resolution/tree building because it runs from a foreign worktree (the machinery has never executed in this configuration — the PR's headline scenario ships with zero verification that a guest actually condenses rather than merely being *selected*); and PrepareCommitMsg/PostCommit set divergence (question 3) — asserting the stamped trailer's checkpoint contains the guest session's metadata pins both hooks to the same resolution in one test.

## Important Improvements (5–7)

**3. Shell interposition against a real process tree — rate 6.** Add a helper-process case (the `PROCTREE_HELPER` TestMain pattern already exists in `proctree_test.go`) spawned via `sh -c`, asserting the child's `Ancestors()` reports an `sh` entry whose `Exe` satisfies `isShellLikeExe`, and that the first non-shell ancestor is the test binary. **6. ## Test Quality Issues

- `TestNewStateStore_RefusesRealRepoUnderGoTest` (`cmd/entire/cli/session/state_test.go`) is environment-coupled: it assumes the package source dir is inside a git repo *and* outside `os.TempDir()`. ## Redundant Tests

Nearly none — the layering is deliberate. Two mild overlaps, both defensible: PID-reuse rejection is tested at the proctree layer (`TestSameProcess_RejectsPIDReuse`) and again through the matcher ("dead process refs cannot match a recycled PID") — keep both, they name different regressions. `TestFindSessionsForCommitLinking_FallsBackToWorktree` is thin (largely implied by the union test plus existing worktree-matcher tests) but cheap and pins the human-commit path through the new entry point; not worth removing.

## Positive Observations

- Every test names its regression (the sessC dangling-trailer incident, the Cursor-bugbot shell-recording finding, PID recycling) — exemplary compliance with the house rule.
- `TestAncestors_ChildSeesParentIdentity` is the right test for the core primitive: a real child process, real JSON round-trip, asserting pid+starttime identity across a process boundary.
- The store guard is tested in both directions (refuses real repo, allows temp repo), and the agentimport repo-scoping assertion was folded into the existing `TestRun_ImportsAndIsIdempotent` rather than a niche file.
- Imported-session exclusion is covered at both matcher layers (identity and worktree), and the liveness tests use real `git worktree add`, not path fakes.

Key files: `/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/session-identity/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_identity.go`, `.../strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` (untested gates at `condenseAndUpdateState` and `updateBaseCommitIfChanged`), `.../strategy/session_identity_test.go`, `.../strategy/manual_commit_worktree_session_test.go` (natural home for gap 1–2), `.../internal/proctree/proctree_test.go` (helper pattern for gap 3).</result>

lines: - **Location-independent transcript resolution** - transcript paths are always computed dynamically from the current repo location (via `agent.GetSessionDir` + `agent.ResolveSessionFile`), never stored in checkpoint metadata. This ensures restore/rewind works after repo relocation or across machines.

- **Token usage scoping** - `SessionState.TokenUsage` is the session-wide total used by `entire status`; `SessionState.CheckpointTokenUsage` is the pending checkpoint delta since the last condensation. Checkpoint metadata must stay scoped to `CheckpointTranscriptStart` or the pending checkpoint delta. Cursor tokens come only from stop-hook payloads, while Copilot CLI can also backfill full-session totals from `session.shutdown`. Condensation's transcript recompute runs with `subagentsDir=""` and so drops `SubagentTokens`; `withSubagentTokensFrom` refills it from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`, and the store sums it across a checkpoint's sessions via `types.AddTokenUsage` (the single token-summing primitive — do not hand-roll another; a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place).
- Tracks session state in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees)

-- **Commit-to-session linking is identity-first** (`strategy/session_identity.go`): session-start hooks record ONLY the agent process — the hook's first non-shell ancestor (pid + start time) — in `SessionState.AgentAncestry`; the chain above it (user shell, tmux, terminal, IDE) is deliberately unrecorded, or a human commit typed in the same terminal would falsely identity-match. Commit hooks walk their own ancestry and link the commit to the session whose agent process is an ancestor — in any worktree (nearest ancestor wins, ties by latest interaction, start times guard PID reuse). The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. A commit identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is guest-linked — condensed and linked, but worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment) is never mutated from a foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching stays as the fallback for commits with no agent ancestry: imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining with a stderr hint naming `entire session adopt`. Under `go test`, `session.NewStateStore` refuses to open outside the temp root so non-isolated tests fail loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo.

+- **Commit-to-session linking is identity-first** (`strategy/session_identity.go`): session-start hooks record ONLY the agent process — the hook's first non-shell ancestor (pid + start time) — in `SessionState.AgentAncestry`; the chain above it (user shell, tmux, terminal, IDE) is deliberately unrecorded, or a human commit typed in the same terminal would falsely identity-match. Commit hooks walk their own ancestry and link the commit to the session whose agent process is an ancestor — in any worktree (nearest ancestor wins, ties by latest interaction, start times guard PID reuse). The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. A commit identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is guest-linked — condensed and linked, but worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment) is never mutated from a foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching is always computed (it is the sole mechanism for commits with no agent ancestry): imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining — the stderr hint naming `entire session adopt` fires only from the commit-linking path, and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either. Under `go test`, `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree` refuse to open outside the temp root so non-isolated tests fail loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo.
- **Shadow branch migration** - if user does stash/pull/rebase (HEAD changes without commit), shadow branch is automatically moved to new base commit
- **Orphaned branch cleanup** - if a shadow branch exists without a corresponding session state file, it is automatically reset when a new session starts
- PrePush hook can push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch alongside user pushes

All review fixes are implemented, lint is clean (0 issues), all platforms cross-compile, and the four affected packages pass. The full unit suite is running in the background; integration + canary follow, then I'll commit and push.

What went in, mapped to the findings:

**Critical fixes:**
- **Guest condensation data corruption** (code-reviewer #1): `condenseAndUpdateState` now takes a full guest branch — transcript condensed, trailer state (`LastCheckpointID`, checkpoint window) updated, then *returns* before any of the three data mutations: no shadow-branch delete mark, no `BaseCommit` advance, no `FilesTouched` clearing. The carry-forward block in the caller is also gated (`isSessionHomeWorktree`), since remaining-files would diff the home shadow tree against the foreign commit and carry-forward reads file content from the wrong worktree.
- **False "none was linked" hint** (both agents): `resolveWorktreeCandidates` no longer prints — it returns an `ambiguous` flag; the hint now lives in `findSessionsForCommitLinking` and fires only when the *final* set (after identity rescue) is empty. Amend and post-rewrite paths stay silent by construction. Pinned by three new subtests: silent decline via the plain matcher, audible decline via the linking path, and rescue-suppresses-hint.

**Important fixes:** negative-path Debug diagnostics at all three silence points (unresolvable ancestry at record and commit time, all-shell chains); `isSessionHomeWorktree` is now a pure comparison taking the caller's already-resolved worktree path — the fail-open error path is structurally gone; `NewStateStoreForWorktree` rejects empty roots and runs the same isolation guard; ancestry refreshes on TurnStart when the recorded agent ref is dead (resume support); one state listing per hook instead of two; `procInfo` consolidation halves per-level introspection calls on every platform (Windows: one snapshot+scan per level instead of two); `tmux: server` and empty-Exe now classify as shell-like; tombstoned sessions excluded from identity matching; import state failure upgraded to Warn with the user-visible symptom named.

**Tests + docs:** guest-gating test in both directions (home advances, guest frozen — the inverse being the scarier regression), stale-decline subtest, `sh -c` real-process proctree test, guard-refusal tests for the new constructor, and all the comment drift fixed (impossible "terminal shell" example, union-vs-fallback framing in three places, slice-headroom clause, Linux reboot caveat).

fix(strategy): address review findings on identity linking

Critical fixes from the review pass:

- Guest-linked condensation no longer touches the home worktree's shadow
  state. The gate previously guarded only the BaseCommit assignment;
  the shadow-branch delete mark, the remaining-files diff (home shadow
  tree vs the FOREIGN commit tree), and carry-forward (which reads file
  content from the committing — wrong — worktree) all still ran, so a
  guest condensation would rebuild the home worktree's shadow branch

input.content:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1061
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

Commit-to-session linking guesses by worktree path: the commit hooks match `SessionState.WorktreePath` against the commit's worktree. Any drift between bookkeeping and reality loses the linkage. This has bitten three times (PR #1647, PR #1287, PR #1991): an agent committing in a sibling worktree gets an unlinked commit — or, with a poisoned state dir, a **wrong** link. The latest instance: `agentimport` tests missing repo isolation leaked fixture sessions (`sessC` et al.) into the developer's real `.git/entire-sessions`; prepare-commit-msg linked a commit to the `sessC` fixture and stamped a trailer whose checkpoint was never written — a dangling trailer, repaired only by manual session-state surgery.

## Change

**Identity-first linking.** An agent-made commit is attributed by *who made it*, not *where it happened*:

- The session-initializing hook records **the agent process only** — its first non-shell ancestor (agents run hooks as children, possibly via `sh -c`) — as a pid+starttime ref in `SessionState.AgentAncestry`. Everything above the agent (user shell, tmux, terminal emulator, IDE) is deliberately unrecorded: it is shared with unrelated processes, and matching it would falsely attribute a human commit typed in the same terminal (Cursor bugbot's high-severity finding on the first cut of this PR). The ref refreshes on TurnStart when the recorded process is dead (resume under a new agent process). New `internal/proctree` package resolves ancestry cross-platform (darwin sysctl, linux `/proc`, windows toolhelp), one introspection call per level; pid+starttime survives PID reuse.
- Commit hooks walk their own ancestry (git ← tool shell ← agent) and match that ref. The match is **unioned** with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement — a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree, and identity adds the one path matching missed.
- **Guest-linking:** a commit identity-matched outside the session's home worktree condenses the transcript and records the trailer state, and touches **nothing else** — no `BaseCommit` advance, no shadow-branch deletion, no carry-forward (which reads file content from the committing — wrong — worktree). Shadow branches are keyed by BaseCommit + WorktreeID; any of those mutations from a foreign worktree corrupts or orphans the home worktree's in-flight state.

Net effect: **an agent commit links to its session in any worktree, automatically** — no `session adopt`, no retro-attach. `adopt` shrinks to its migration role.

**Hardened worktree fallback** (human commits, severed process trees):
- Imported sessions never link (historical records; a leaked imported fixture is exactly what hijacked the sessC commit).
- Multi-worktree ambiguity filters to sessions that interacted within 15 minutes: one live worktree links; two live worktrees still decline — never guess. The decline is announced on **stderr with the remedy** (`entire session adopt`), but only from the commit-linking path and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either; amend and post-rewrite stay silent.
- Identity failure is diagnosable: unresolvable ancestry (restricted `/proc`, sandbox denials) and all-shell chains log at Debug at both record and match time, so "identity never works on this host" is visible in a doctor bundle instead of being masked by the fallback forever.

**Leak closed at both ends:**
- `agentimport` scopes its session-state writes to the repo being imported into (new `session.NewStateStoreForWorktree`, which rejects empty roots) instead of the process CWD — a production bug, not just a test bug.
- Under `go test`, both store constructors refuse to open outside the temp root, so any future non-isolated test **fails loudly** instead of writing fixtures into a real repo. The full unit suite (8,973) passes with the guard on — the agentimport tests were the only leakers in the repo.

## Review history on this PR

- Cursor bugbot (high severity, valid): raw ancestor-chain recording captured the user's shell/terminal → same-terminal human commits falsely matched. Fixed by the one-non-shell-ref recorder (`b38c45c6a`).
- Four-agent toolkit review (`f561bab64`): guest condensation previously still ran the shadow-delete/remaining-files/carry-forward paths with cross-worktree data (critical, fixed); the adopt hint printed before identity rescue, false-positively, twice per commit, and on amend/rebase (critical, fixed); plus negative-path diagnostics, pure `isSessionHomeWorktree`, TurnStart ancestry refresh, store-guard coverage for the explicit-root constructor, single state listing per hook, halved proctree call counts, `tmux: server`/empty-exe classification, tombstone exclusion, and comment/doc drift.

## Testing

- `internal/proctree`: real-process tests incl. helper-process round-trips proving a child sees its parent's pid+starttime identity, directly and through `sh -c` interposition; cross-compiled and vetted for linux/windows (note for reviewers: Windows code is exercised for real only by CI's Windows job).
- Strategy unit: ancestry recording; identity matching (worktree-independence, PID-reuse rejection, imported + tombstone exclusion, latest-interaction tiebreak); union semantics; guest gating in both directions (home advances `BaseCommit`, guest frozen); hint ordering (silent plain matcher / audible linking path / rescue suppresses); liveness disambiguation incl. all-stale; shell-filter table incl. `tmux: server` and empty exe.
- Session/agentimport: store guards (both constructors), repo-scoped import state.
- `mise run fmt` clean, `mise run lint` 0 issues, full unit suite 8,973 pass, integration suite 480 pass, Vogon canary green.

## Known gap / product calls for the reviewer

- **No end-to-end test where a guest session's shadow content actually condenses across worktrees.** Guest *selection* and *state gating* are unit-pinned in both directions, but the full condensation flow from a foreign worktree (tree building, checkpoint content) has never executed in a test — it needs SaveStep scaffolding and is scoped as follow-up. This is the highest-value test still missing.
- The 15-minute liveness window (`recentSessionWindow`) and the shell-blocklist approach (vs. positive agent identification) are judgment calls — flag if you'd pick differently.
- Guest-linked checkpoints attribute the transcript correctly but file attribution diffs against the foreign commit; documented as the v1 boundary.

message.content: is this changning logic from worktree logic to sessions to making it better like we saw from when we were making a commit in this session and then it didn't link

content.text:
Yes — exactly that. The thing that bit us twice in this session is the thing this PR fixes, and our own incidents are literally the regression story in the tests and commit message.

**What happened to us, mechanically:** this session's state file says `worktree_path: .worktrees/pr-review`. When I committed in `.worktrees/checkpoint-capture` (and later `.worktrees/session-identity`), the commit hook asked "which session lives in *this* worktree?" — path comparison, nothing else. Answer: none (or worse, the leaked `sessC` fixture). So: no link, or a dangling trailer, and I had to do the manual repoint-replay-restore dance three times.

**What changes:** the question itself. Instead of only "which session is *recorded here*?", the hook now also asks "**which session's agent process is my parent?**" When the session started, its hook recorded my Claude Code process (pid + start time). When I run `git commit` — in *any* worktree — the commit hook walks up its own process tree: git ← shell ← Claude. That Claude process matches the recorded ref, so the commit links to this session, deterministically. Worktree bookkeeping can't drift because it's no longer load-bearing for agent commits — the process tree *is* the truth about who made the commit.

**Worktree logic isn't replaced, it's demoted and repaired.** It still runs on every commit (it must — concurrent sessions in the commit's own worktree belong in the checkpoint, and human commits have no agent in their process tree at all). But it's no longer the only signal, and its own failure modes got fixed along the way: leaked/imported fixtures can never be chosen again, and the "two candidate worktrees, give up" case now prefers the session that interacted seconds ago over one idle for days — the other half of what would have saved us.

Replaying this exact session under the new code: my commit in `session-identity` → ancestry finds Claude → session guest-linked → trailer stamped, transcript condensed, checkpoint real — and per the review-hardening, it does all that *without* touching the session's pr-review-side state, so nothing over here breaks either. Zero manual steps.

The one honest asterisk: it only works once the fixed binary is the one running the hooks — which is why even this PR's own commits still needed the manual procedure. Last time, on its own behalf.

Agreed — and that's the right framing for the PR too: this isn't an enhancement, it's restoring the baseline invariant that should have held all along. "A commit made by an agent session belongs to that session" is table stakes for a tool whose whole premise is that commits carry their session context. Everything we did manually this week — the repoint-replay-restore dance, the dangling-trailer forensics — was compensating for that invariant not holding, and the fact that *the tool's own development sessions* kept tripping over it is the strongest evidence it was a baseline defect rather than an edge case.

The binary caveat wasn't meant as a hedge on the design — it's just the ordinary deployment lag every hook fix has (same as #1987's hint: correct on merge, active once the release lands in people's hooks). Once #2013 ships, this is simply how linking works, invisibly, everywhere: worktree matching handles the common case as before, identity quietly catches everything that used to fall through, and `session adopt` returns to being a migration tool instead of a repair kit.

So the ready-for-review answer stands, with this sharpened pitch for whoever reviews it: the PR makes the tool's core promise actually hold under the multi-worktree workflows the team itself uses daily.
